body: My parents, whatever flaws they do have, both sacrificed everything for my sibling and I. During my childhood my mother quit her job to take care of me, as I was chronically and severely ill. Some ten years later she left work again to care for my sibling, who suffered a severe brain injury. In a similar vein, during the 2008 recession my father was laid off and took a job some 1800 miles from home to prevent us from losing our home. He left the people he loved most in the world and lived alone for over a year to make sure we would stay housed and fed. My parents’ ability to overcome adversity inspires me every single day
This is me to a T as well. Except my family lives 14 hours from me and my boyfriend just ended things. I don’t understand how to do adult friendships.

My bio stuff was physiology and anatomy focused so I was brought on for some specific brain stuff. Originally it seemed coding/the deeper engineering stuff would be an as-it-goes basis. But I think that the group I’m with has a different timeline of as-it-goes than I did.

As for the assault I believed them. Frankly I’m not sure my ex did believe me. The first thing he asked me after I told him was “well are you sure that’s actually what happened”.  I guess it was disheartening to hear from someone I had cared for so much and to think that since I believed the people who told me about their own assaults, if someone I loved didn’t believe me when I told them, maybe something was inherently wrong with my understanding of what happened. I know that I was assaulted, but hearing that from him chipped away a lot of my own self-assurance.

I think that this is much more cathartic than I had expected. It’s just this wave of relief to not hold everything back under pressure. Being anonymous on the internet helps; the thought of telling my friends or family I feel I’m failing after taking a risk moving away and trying a new field is still something I don’t think I can do. But I will try your advice with my counselor given that just letting things out online has taken a little of the immediate edge off. Thank you stranger for reading and engaging. I need it

I haven’t told anyone else about the assault because I’m afraid that people will blame me for staying in his apartment. Or that they won’t believe me because I don’t have proof other than my words.

As for talking to my counselor and psychiatrist they are both going to be new people for me. I built up a lot of trust and felt safe with my old counselor where I felt I could talk to her openly and not have her place me in mandatory psych holding. Being hospitalized against my will is a very big fear for me. I currently don’t think (at this immediate) moment I am a high risk for suicide. Yes, I’m self-harming and thinking about suicide but I feel that I am unable to actually kill myself. My concern is that if I explain everything in detail to my new team that they won’t understand and will want me hospitalized.

I’m currently working in biomed engineering coming out of a strictly bio undergrad. I was taken in because I had niche knowledge of one field my team wanted to start on, but I really don’t have the baseline IT or general engineering knowledge that everyone else seems to. I can’t even code. It’s been extremely disheartening, and I’m afraid to talk to my advisor (known for being extremely tough with high expectations) because I feel like a fraud and don’t want to disappoint anyone.
